title: Onboarding Eval: Compactness & Escape Heuristics Prompt Exercise
body:
Purpose:
This is a working prompt-set for model-onboarding that focuses on two orthogonal stress axes: compactness (minified vs pretty output) and escape/encoding heuristics (unicode, control chars, nested-JSON-as-string, etc.). Goal is to detect subtle regressions that cause downstream JSON parsers or consumers to fail silently or to require brittle post-processing.

Scope and motivation:
- For Redwood’s serving runtime we often rely on strict JSON outputs for routing, ingestion, caching keys, and downstream typed consumers. Small changes in model tokens or decoding settings have caused real production issues (examples: extra trailing spaces in keys, optional quotes omitted in non-strict generations, wrong escaping for U+2028/U+2029, unescaped backslashes inside string fields).
- This prompt exercise is targeted at onboarding new model variants (quantized, distilled) to ensure they match expected output surface and to expose heuristics that can be fixed by prompt engineering, decoding constraints, or post-filtering.

Quick summary of what to measure per run:
- Parse success rate (json.loads equivalent)
- Schema conformance rate (all required keys present + types match)
- Minified vs pretty fidelity (does the model produce compact JSON when asked)
- Escape correctness (escape sequences valid, no unescaped control chars)
- Regression signal: new failure modes compared to baseline model snapshot (per test case diff)
- Token and latency overhead for enforced formatting prompts (tokens consumed by instructions vs payload)

Reference schema (simple, flat primary object used for tests):
- name: string
- id: integer (32-bit)
- tags: array of strings (may be empty)
- payload: object { text: string, meta: string (optional, may contain escaped JSON) }
- score: number | null

Note: schema presented as plain text here for readability in Drive; canonical JSON Schema lives in linked_artifacts.

Prompt templates (three variants):
1) Minified enforcement (shorter instruction):
"Please output EXACTLY one JSON object and nothing else. Minify it (no whitespace except inside string values). Schema: name (string), id (int), tags (array[string]), payload {text, meta?}, score (number|null). Do not include backticks or explanation text."

2) Pretty enforcement (human readable):
"Return a pretty-printed JSON object with 2-space indentation. Include only the keys defined in the schema. For payload.meta, if you must include JSON, embed it as an escaped string. No extra commentary."

3) Escape stress (explicit escapes + invisible chars):
"Generate one JSON object following the schema. In 'payload.text' include examples that exercise escaping mechanics: a new line, an emoji, U+2028 line separator, zero-width joiner, a JSON snippet that contains quotes and backslashes (it should be embedded as an escaped string), and a numeric-like string that starts with +. Ensure output is valid JSON parsable by strict parsers."

Test case bank (each case to be run against prompt templates above):
- TC1: Basic happy path (simple ASCII name, id 42, tags ["perf"], payload.text short)
- TC2: Long name (>1000 chars) with embedded quotes and slashes -> checks string-length handling + tokenization overhead
- TC3: Unicode separators: include U+2028 and U+2029 in payload.text (some JS parsers choke if not escaped)
- TC4: Zero-width joiners + RTL mark mixing with emoji in payload.text
- TC5: Nested JSON-as-string in payload.meta: '{\"stage\":\"prod\", \"cfg\": {\"k\": \"v\\\\\"}}' (note deep escaping)
- TC6: Array heterogeneity: tags contains numbers represented without quotes by some models (should be strings)
- TC7: Trailing comma temptation: prompt asks pretty JSON but model emits trailing commas after last item
- TC8: Duplicate keys with different case ("ID" and "id") -> canonicalization check
- TC9: Scientific notation and BigInt-looking values for id and score -> ensure id integer check fails as expected, score accepts numeric formats but flagged if Infinity/NaN
- TC10: Injection stress: prompt includes example output enclosed in backticks in the instruction; model echoes the backticked example verbatim (should not)

Expected/acceptance heuristics:
- Strict parse (primary gate): json.loads equivalent must succeed. Any parse failure = fail.
- Schema gate: types and required keys must pass. Optional payload.meta may be empty string or absent.
- Escape gate: output must not contain raw U+2028/U+2029 characters unescaped if the backend consumer is JS; flag them as WARNING for languages that allow them but FAIL for JS ingestion tests.
- Compactness gate: when asked to minify, whitespace outside of string values must be <= 1KB for this simple schema; if model returns pretty output in minified mode, mark as FAIL.

Example expected outputs (minified):
{"name":"db-migrator","id":7,"tags":["deploy","slo"],"payload":{"text":"migration completed","meta":"{\\\"ver\\\":\\\"1.2\\\"}"},"score":0.87}

Example pretty output:
{
  "name": "db-migrator",
  "id": 7,
  "tags": [
    "deploy",
    "slo"
  ],
  "payload": {
    "text": "migration completed",
    "meta": "{\\\"ver\\\":\\\"1.2\\\"}"
  },
  "score": 0.87
}

Regression capture & triage notes:
- Capture raw model output, tokenizer tokens around boundary characters (quotes, backslashes), and the deterministic seed used for deterministic decoding (if any).
- Diff new failure traces against baseline snapshot (GH: redwood-inference/eval-suites#snapshot-2025-01-01).
- For escape failures, small prompt edits have historically fixed issues (explicitly wrap JSON sample in triple-escaped string in instruction). If prompt fixes are brittle, consider post-filtering layer in serving runtime that normalizes known escape patterns.

Operational checklist for onboarding run:
- Run each prompt template x5 seeds at temperature=0.0, 0.2, 0.5 (15 runs per test case) to surface temperature-dependent failures.
- Record parse success, schema pass, token usage, latency, and any post-processing diffs.
- Flag any run that increases failed parse rate by >1% relative to baseline as a regression candidate.

Open questions / TODOs (notes-to-self):
- Do we want to treat U+2028/U+2029 as FAIL universally or per-ingestion-target? (prod JS vs Python consumers differ)
- Evaluate adding a small constrained-decoder pass that enforces ASCII-only for key names (might reduce model expressiveness).
- Add canonical test harness code snippet for SRE to run in CI and annotate failing examples with a suggested remediation (prompt, post-filter, config).

Links / references:
- See linked artifacts for canonical JSON Schema and CI integration ticket.
- Example flaky incident: slack thread #incidents -> message ID 12345 (production outage due to unescaped line separator causing frontend to drop event).

Notes to reviewer:
This document is intentionally pragmatic and workshop-style. Expect iterative updates as we run this against new model candidates (quantized L2 variants). Add test cases you observe in the wild by appending to the bank with a short reproduction snippet and affected consumer (e.g., frontend-router, metrics-pusher, embed-cache).

---
Local checklist before marking final: run full sweep, capture failing examples into GH issue with model id, attach tokenizer debug dump, and propose either (1) prompt fix, (2) small parser normalization, or (3) model reject to onboarding.
